## How to read this

Every claim below was run, grepped or queried on 2026-09-22. Three features have been burned
planning against specs instead of code, so nothing here is inherited from an earlier spec. Where a
claim contradicts a written decision, both are stated and the contradiction is the finding.

## The findings that change the spec

### F1 — The canonical logo has one lab's name compiled into it

`packages/ui/src/components/LogoChip.tsx` renders `<span style={LOGOTYPE_STYLE}>CITE BAURU</span>`
as a **string literal**. Its docstring states feature 001's US4 as a rule: *"every surface renders
**this**, never a per-page image. So the component takes no `src`, no `variant="image"`, and no way
to substitute artwork: the only choice a call site has is which palette colour the chip is printed
on."* The decision is dated — `visual-identity.md` § Logo, round 2, 2026-08-23.

**So the co-branding gap is not the one spec.md described.** FR-014 assumed the problem was that
`theme.logoUrl` is never rendered. The real problem is worse and simpler: **every page of every
organization renders the words `CITE BAURU`**, and the component is explicitly designed to refuse
image substitution. A second lab would not have a missing logo; it would have *someone else's*.

The component already anticipates per-organization variation on one axis — `LogoChipColour`
includes `primary`, documented as *"the accent — the only pink this library has, and a
per-organization one (CLR-001): a co-branded poster chip, **never the header**"*. So the designed
customisation point is colour, and the header is explicitly excluded from it.

**Consequence for the plan**: FR-014's mechanism has to change, and the change must not break
001's US4. See plan § D3.

### F2 — CITe's name is compiled into the admin panel as well

`payload.config.ts` sets `admin.meta.titleSuffix: '— Fab Lab CITe Bauru'`. A second lab's
administrators would work in a panel titled with CITe's name. This is the same defect as F1 in a
second place, which is exactly the shape memory records as *"a requirement applied to an inventory
instead of as a rule"* — the fifth recurring class. Any fix for F1 that enumerates call sites will
miss this one unless the requirement is stated as a rule.

### F3 — No organization carries a logo or hero URL, and none carries a quota

Queried on 2026-09-22:

```text
id    | slug                  | has_logo | has_hero | storage_quota_mb | storage_used_mb
34686 | seed-economy-cite     | f        | f        | (null)           | 0
34687 | seed-economy-tuned    | f        | f        | (null)           | 0
34688 | seed-economy-untouched| f        | f        | (null)           | 0
```

- **No text value has to be migrated** when `logoUrl`/`heroImageUrl` change type. The field change
  is clean.
- **`storageQuotaMb` is NULL on every row**, which is FR-033's backfill and confirms the column has
  never been used by anything.
- The rows are test fixtures; the CITe organization is absent because the suite recreates the world.
  That is the recorded behaviour of this database, not a new problem.

### F4 — `syncCounter` CAN write a global collection, but not as the uploading user

Two independent facts, both verified:

1. **`buildTenantClient` applies no tenant constraint to a `global` collection** — the clause is
   built as `isScoped(collection) ? { tenant: { equals: tenantId } } : undefined`. So
   `organizations` is reachable by id through the choke point; the target is not unreachable.
2. **`organizations.update` is `masterOnly()`**, and the request-scoped client runs
   `overrideAccess: false` with the session user. A maker uploading a photo therefore cannot write
   `storageUsedMb`, and neither can a staff member.

`CounterDeps.getStore` is the seam that resolves this, and it has a **precedent in shipped code**:
its docstring says *"Injected by tests and by FR-016's path"* — the anonymous download counter
already injects `getPublicCounterStore`, a narrow store built inside `lib/tenancy/`. The quota's
write takes the same shape with a different client.

### F5 — `CounterField` is a closed union and the gate scans by `admin.readOnly`

`CounterField` is `'curtidas' | 'downloads' | 'totalModelos' | 'xpTotal' | 'nivel'`.
`tests/content/counters.test.ts` widens it locally to `DerivedField = CounterField | 'formatos' |
'skills'`, then `unaccountedDerivedFields` walks **every collection in the built config** and every
`flattenedFields` entry, reporting any field with `admin.readOnly` that is neither reconciled here
nor listed in `NOT_AN_FR020_DERIVED`.

`storageUsedMb` carries `admin: { readOnly: true }`, which is *why* it needs today's exemption.
Deleting the exemption (FR-031) therefore requires, in the same change: widening `CounterField`,
teaching the gate how the value is recomputed, and removing the `NOT_AN_FR020_DERIVED` entry.
Doing any one without the others turns the gate red rather than green.

### F6 — The quota cannot be enforced from `refuseOffPolicyUpload` without a named tenancy export

`refuseOffPolicyUpload` lives in `apps/web/collections/Media.ts`, outside `lib/tenancy/`, and
`eslint.config.mjs` fences `lib/tenancy/system-payload*` and `lib/tenancy/unscoped*` from import
anywhere else. So the hook cannot reach the system client directly; it must call a **named export
from `lib/tenancy/`** whose consumers are enumerated — the same arrangement
`getPublicCounterStore` already uses for the anonymous download write.

This is a seventh enumerated consumer of the dangerous client, arriving from a direction spec.md
did not anticipate. It is *not* the widening CLR-005 declined: that one would have let a human
actor read the tenant collection, whereas this is a server-side guard reading two numeric columns
of the organization the request is already confined to.

### F7 — The Home's hero is the LCP element with 236 ms of headroom

006's merged CI run measured `/` at **2264 ms against a 2500 ms budget**; the five sibling public
pages sit at 1765–1780 ms. The hero is served today as two static local files,
`HERO_AVIF_SRCSET` and `HERO_WEBP_SRCSET`, with a dedicated mobile crop and honest `w` descriptors.

An arbitrary per-organization hero served from object storage changes the origin, the format
guarantee, the cache headers and the existence of a mobile crop — every property the current
measurement depends on. **The budget cannot absorb an unconstrained uploaded image**, and
`scripts/lcp-budget.sh` measures CITe's own Home, so a regression would appear on the lab that did
not upload anything.

### F8 — `presign.ts` is the standing example of a module with tests and no caller

`lib/uploads/presign.ts` expresses the per-group presign policy and has 20 passing tests. The only
reference to it anywhere in the tree is `tests/uploads/presign.test.ts`. It has been dead since
002's D1 turned `clientUploads` off. It is named here because a quota module is the obvious next
one, and because it is evidence the class recurs after being written down.

### F9 — The plugin sets `tenant` from the admin's cookie, after `beforeOperation` has run

`@payloadcms/plugin-multi-tenant@3.88.0`'s `tenantField` gives the `tenant` relationship a
`defaultValue` function whose body reads **`getTenantFromCookie(req.headers, idType)`** — the admin's
tenant-selector cookie. Two consequences:

1. **The tenant of a write is not the host.** `seed-on-create.ts` documents the same thing from the
   other side: a master creates organization B *while being served on some other host*.
2. **A `defaultValue` is applied during field processing**, which runs *after* `beforeOperation`.
   So `args.data.tenant` is absent in a `beforeOperation` hook on a create.

Measured 2026-09-27, while repairing review round 1. Any guard needing the target organization must
read it from the document under write, at a hook where the field defaults have been applied.

### F10 — A derived value may be reconciled by the gate without being a `syncCounter` field

`counters.ts` says of `formatos`: *"derived on its own document and is not a counter"*. Neither
`formatos` nor `skills` appears in `CounterField`; both appear in the gate's own
`DerivedField = CounterField | 'formatos' | 'skills'`, and neither is ever passed to `syncCounter`
anywhere in the tree (grepped).

**This is the precedent `storageUsedMb` fits**, and it is why D4 needs neither a new derivation kind
nor a widening of `CounterField`.

## Existing patterns this feature should follow

- **A narrow named store, built inside `lib/tenancy/`, for a privileged operation with a bounded
  reach** — `getPublicCounterStore` (one column of one row, every other operation throws) and
  `getPublicLabLevelStore` (two collections, forced projection, no `where`). Both refuse rather
  than filter, and both carry the argument in a docstring rather than in a commit message.
- **A derived column is recomputed from its sources inside the writing transaction**, never
  incremented, wherever source rows exist — `counters.ts`'s `count`/`sum` versus `delta`, with the
  read-modify-write window documented as the price of `delta`.
- **A refusal carries the offending value and the expected shape** — both existing refusals in
  `refuseOffPolicyUpload` name the file, the measured property and the policy.
- **A non-null column with a default arrives with a migration that backfills**, and the `.json`
  snapshot is produced by `./scripts/migrate-create.sh` — the `destaqueHome` shape from 006.
- **A test asserts the thing that was deliberately NOT done**, so a later widening is loud —
  006's FR-035 (rows are not links) and this feature's FR-018.
